history.rationale: reproducing test FAILS on buggy and PASSES on fixed; numerical probes are disabled (--no-probes), so the test transition is the whole of the evidence

plans.objective: Rebuild buggy and fixed pandas revisions identically as compiled builds (Cython extensions), then run the developer test selection with the file path on both, so that test_nanops_reductions_dont_skip_nan_with_mask and test_nansem_partial_mask_no_skipna_is_per_slice fail on buggy (real assertion failure, nansem returning scalar nan) and pass on fixed.
assumptions: The harness default CPython is acceptable for this pandas era (the issue used Python 3.14.3; the fix's pandas version and commit date are not stated, so no python_version or NumPy pin is set).
If the build fails with a native/compiler error, the next iteration should adjust the build (pins or python_version) rather than the test.
Using -k with the file path and an 'or' expression selects both named cases, which avoids the file::case node-id problem for class methods.

actions.step: Rebuild buggy revision as a compiled package (Cython extensions) on the harness default CPython, with no pins, so the build uses the era-appropriate default NumPy/Cython resolution.
Rebuild fixed revision with the identical recipe so the comparison is like for like.
Run the developer test selection on the buggy revision; expected to FAIL with a real assertion (nansem returns scalar nan, not per-slice array).
Run the same developer test selection on the fixed revision; expected to PASS.

plans.success_criterion: The developer test selection fails on buggy with a genuine assertion failure (not collection/setup error) and passes on fixed, with both revisions built by the same compiled recipe.
